note: Cross-model control (non-clinical general-purpose model, vs BioMistral-7B). Same GA hyperparameters as the BioMistral pilot (lr=2e-6, max_steps=8), required LoRA (BIOUNLEARN_USE_LORA=1) -- full fine-tuning OOM'd on this 8B model at the same settings that worked for 7B BioMistral.
note2: No collapse (train_loss -1.76, controlled, unlike BioMistral's original -222 collapse at higher lr) -- own baseline (pre-GA) eval running separately to make this comparable, since Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct was never fine-tuned on BioUnlearn-Bench and its pre-unlearning FA/DEF numbers will differ substantially from BioMistral's.
interpretation: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct's own baseline FA is much LOWER than BioMistral-7B's baseline (RGU 0.483 vs 0.741; IFE 0.768 vs 0.839) -- i.e. the general instruct model already fails to reproduce the exact forget_answer text more often at baseline than the clinically-tuned model does, before any unlearning is applied. Counterintuitive if read as 'BioMistral knows clinical facts better' (you'd expect that to mean MORE verbatim reproduction, i.e. LOWER baseline FA, not higher) -- more likely reflects ROUGE-based FA being sensitive to phrasing/style overlap with the benchmark's answer text, not pure factual correctness, and BioMistral's clinical-domain phrasing happening to diverge more from the benchmark's specific answer style. Post-GA movement on Llama is small (RGU FA +0.0345 = exactly 2/58, same noise-floor caveat as the OGDA results) and roughly comparable in magnitude to BioMistral's own gentle-GA movement. This is a single pilot run, not yet a real cross-model comparison of entanglement severity -- would need the full baseline x GA/NPO/RMU matrix on Llama, not just one GA run, before concluding whether clinical entanglement is BioMistral-specific.
